problem: Learned navigation policies consume past observations as a time-ordered sequence or recurrent state, so earlier traversals or other robots' experience cannot be reused, and memory cost scales with history length. Systems that do reuse experience build an explicit map or topological graph and plan on it, or use memory only to pick goals.
motivation: Robots operating repeatedly in the same environment accumulate long streams of pose-stamped observations. A learned planner that plans directly over this experience, without a separately maintained map, would be simpler and could fuse frames from different trajectories. The observation driving the paper is that the natural index of an observation is where it was taken rather than when.
key_idea: Represent the environment as an unordered set of depth keyframes indexed by camera pose, and plan with a transformer that uses pose (x, y, heading) as rotary positional embedding so attention depends only on pose differences.
insight: The gain comes from the pose RoPE rather than the architecture: replacing it with temporal RoPE (VNT-TA) drops overall SPL by 6.5 points, and the gap grows with geodesic distance (4.6 to 17.1 SPL points). Pose as an input feature (VNT-PF) is also worse (86.5 vs 90.4 SPL). Pose RoPE reaches 80% SPL in about 5k steps while the other transformer variants need more than 20k. Poses alone give 66.4% SR, so the depth features carry the geometry the planner needs. Recurrent baselines (LSTM, SRU) fail at about 30% SR, showing that a fixed-size state is a poor environment representation.
method: Spatial context: a set S={(e_i,p_i)} of per-frame feature tokens indexed by camera pose (x,y,yaw), replacing a temporal sequence as the environment memory.

Pose RoPE: rotary embedding applied per pose component. Position frequencies are scaled by s=0.25 m with base b=100. Heading uses integer frequencies (a Fourier series in the heading difference). Attention is invariant to world-frame translation, and rotation invariance is learned via random world-frame rotation augmentation.

Frame embedding and keyframe filter: a frozen DeFM ViT-S/14 encodes each depth frame into 16x16 patch tokens, and a learned attention-pooling summarizer compresses them to one token. Frames are kept only if they add at least η=10 new view-direction-tagged voxels, which keeps 21% of frames.
Goal-aware context: a learned goal token stamped at the goal position joins the context and passes through L_map=6 bidirectional self-attention blocks with pose RoPE.

Query and read-out: a query token built from goal distance and bearing (cos, sin) is stamped at the robot pose and cross-attends the goal-aware context through L_read=4 blocks. It sees no current observation.
Action decoder: an autoregressive GRU decodes a chunk of H=8 discrete actions and the robot executes h=4 before re-querying.
Training: behavior cloning with cross-entropy against a Habitat shortest-path expert on the ground-truth mesh, with pose noise (±0.1 m, ±0.2 rad) and downweighting of near-straight episodes.

setting.backbone: DeFM ViT-S/14 (frozen depth encoder) + 74.3M-parameter pose-RoPE transformer planner with GRU action decoder (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: 800 HM3D scenes; 3,834 frontier-exploration depth-frame bags (about 313 frames each); expert shortest-path actions sampled at 3,000 tasks per step for 30k steps (about 4 h on one L40S)
setting.observation: pre-collected depth keyframes with known camera poses, plus robot planar pose and goal position; no current view
setting.action_space: discrete FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN ±30° / STOP, in chunks of 8 with 4 executed
setting.privileged: Prior exploration depth frames with ground-truth poses (also GT localization in the main results); GT mesh used only for expert supervision in training

numbers_note: No standard benchmark numbers; the paper uses its own HM3D point-goal setup with a pre-explored spatial context, so these are not comparable to the standard HM3D-PointNav leaderboard.
results: VNT-PA reaches 93.3% SR and 90.4% SPL, beating the Causal Transformer (90.3/87.3), VNT-PF (89.5/86.5), VNT-TA (87.1/83.9), and the LSTM and SRU baselines (about 30% SR). With all exploration frames plus robot views, SR reaches 97.1%. Under pose noise VNT-PA loses 8.0 SR points versus 42.1 for OctoMap+A*.
limitations: Planning is 2D only, with discrete actions and simulation only; there is no real-robot test.
Localization error is modeled as independent per-step noise rather than accumulating drift.
The task is purely geometric point-goal navigation, without semantic or language goals, and it needs prior exploration frames with known poses.
